newsitem.title: USA: Republican voters narrow gap in Florida.
newsitem.headline: Republican voters narrow gap in Florida.

text.p: Democrats hold a lead among registered voters in Florida but Republicans are closing the gap, according to the final tally Monday of those eligible to vote in the November elections.
Democrats account for 3.73 million or just over 46 percent of Florida's 8.07 million voters. Republicans account for 3.31 million or 40.1 percent, their largest share ever.

In the last year, the number of registered Democrats has grown by about 15 percent while the number of registered Republicans has grown by more than 20 percent. Party officials said migration patterns are behind the trend.

"You'll see that in a lot of places in the South, just because you've got a lot of retirees that are moving from Northern cities. They tend to be a little more conservative," said Florida Democratic Party spokeswoman Jo Maglino.

Florida Republican Party spokesman Bob Sparks said there had been some switching of party affiliations but primarily, "more voters moving down here associate themselves with the message of the Republicans."
"What you're seeing is the motor voter registrants, who more often than not are picking no political party," he said.

The biggest voter increase was among those registering as independents or "other." While overall registration has grown by about 23 percent over the year in Florida, their numbers grew by 83.5 percent. Independents and "others" now account for 1.04 million, or nearly 13 percent of Florida voters.
The motor voter law enabled voters to register at drivers license bureaus and food stamp offices, drawing in many people who traditionally have not voted, party officials said.

Some analysts questioned how much party affiliation means anyway. Democrats have always outnumbered Republicans in Florida but the Republican presidential candidate has carried the state in every election since 1976.
This year, however, Democrat Bill Clinton was running neck-and-neck with Republican Bob Dole for Florida's 25 electoral votes, the fourth largest total in the nation.
